name: Middle part / curtains / textured crop trends

lead: Curtains are a long fringe parted in the middle, with shorter sides. Together with textured crops they are among the trending men's cuts discussed online.
History sources trace the look to early 20th century Britain and revivals since the 1980s; no studies test its effect on attractiveness.

paras: Fans say the fringe frames the face and covers the forehead or sides of the head. This is a styling claim, not a studied mechanism.
No health risks are reported for the cuts themselves.

lead: Curtains is a hairstyle with a long fringe divided by a middle or side parting, usually with shorter sides and back [1]. In recent years it has been associated with K-pop artists, and middle parts and textured crops are discussed as current men's cuts.

Looksmaxxing forum users debate whether curtains or other cuts flatter facial proportions. No clinical studies exist on these trends, and the sources available document curtains' history more than any appearance outcome [1].
infobox: Long fringe with middle or side part [1]
Late 1980s; 1990s; K-pop association in recent years [1]

paras: The Baiyue of the first millennium BCE are said to have worn short curtained hair. In early 20th century Britain, a long-on-top undercut variant was popular with working-class youth and street gangs, including the Neds in Glasgow, the Scuttlers of Manchester and the Peaky Blinders of Birmingham [1]. A centrally parted style derived from the bowl cut returned in the late 1980s among new wave and synthpop fans, and actors such as Brendan Fraser wore it in the 1990s [1].
K-pop members including those of BTS, Monsta X and NCT are linked to the style in recent years [1].

Users on looksmax.org have posted threads comparing curtains, fringe and other cuts, with some arguing hair choice can offset perceived weaknesses such as narrow eye spacing or a large forehead. Individual users also debate whether curtains add apparent head width.
